Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pipeflow 0.6.0

Breaking changes

  • pip_add() and pip_replace() now signal an error for params whose names are no arguments of the step function, unless the function has a ... argument that takes them.
  • The argument after of pip_add() moved to the end, after exec, so that pip_add() and pip_replace() share the order x, step, fun, tags, params, exec. A call that gave after by position must name it now.
  • params of pip_add() and pip_replace() override the defaults of fun again, as before 0.4.0 (in 0.5.0 the defaults won and pip_add() warned). They must be a list with unique names, and the params of a step list the arguments of fun first, followed by the other params.
  • pip_set_params() on a view sets the values in every step of the pipeline that has the param, also outside the view, so that a param keeps one value. scope = "view" gives the old behavior. An option named scope in ... no longer reaches the methods of pip_param_value<-().
  • .self is released when a step returns, so that step outputs no longer keep the pipeline alive. A function returned by a step that refers to .self fails with object '.self' not found when it is called after the run.
  • A step that changes its own function, params or exec mode while it runs (via .self), or that a later step changes during the run, now ends the run as "outdated" instead of "done" and runs again in the next run, as do the steps that ran with its output.
  • In a run with on_error = "continue", a step mapped over partitioned inputs fails per partition key: its output keeps the results of the keys that succeeded, and each failed key holds a pipeflow_failure with the field key. The step gets state "failed". Mapped steps downstream are not run for the failed keys, unless they take the input via ~try(). The pipeflow_run_failed warning has a new field keys.
  • The deprecated aliases pip_collect_out() and pip_get_graph() were removed. Use pip_collect() and pip_graph().
  • pipeflow no longer re-exports the data.table operators %like%, %ilike%, %flike%, %plike%, %chin%, %between%, %inrange% and %notin%. They still work in the filters of [, e.g. p[tags %like% "model"], without attaching data.table. To use them elsewhere, call library(data.table).

New features

  • Pipelines as functions: as.function() turns a pipeline into a function whose arguments are the unbound params of the pipeline, so that a pipeline can be a step of another pipeline, e.g. pip_add(outer, "step", as.function(inner), params = list(df = ~split)). The exec modes map it over partitions, and the function keeps one inner pipeline per outer step and partition key, so that a changed param only reruns the affected inner steps. out can be a function that is called with a light copy of the run inner pipeline, on_error = "continue" continues the inner run, lgr sets the logger of the inner run, and cache = FALSE switches the kept pipelines off. New pip_inner(x, step) returns the inner pipelines kept by such a step, e.g. to debug an inner run. See ?as.function.pipeflow and the “Nested pipelines” vignette.
  • pip_add() takes a pipeline or view as step and copies its steps, with their functions, params, tags and exec modes, but without their upstream steps: references are resolved by step name in the target pipeline, e.g. pip_add(p, q[c("fit", "plot")]). If a step can’t be added, the pipeline is left unchanged.
  • pip_clone(out = ) copies a pipeline with the outputs of the named steps only, e.g. to send the results of a run back from a parallel worker.
  • pip_output_value() is a generic for annotating the output of a step when the step returns, e.g. to stamp a result with the step it came from and the time of the run. `pip_param_value<-`() is the write side of pip_param_value(): pip_set_params() uses it to keep the annotations of a stored object when it is given a plain value, and passes ... on to its methods. It determines the values for all affected steps before it changes anything, and reports all failures at once with an error of class pipeflow_set_params_error. See the vignette “Annotated step outputs”.
  • pip_set_params() can bind params to steps: a one-sided formula as value, e.g. pip_set_params(p, list(model = ~fit)), binds the param in all selected, unlocked steps that have it unbound, as a formula does in the defaults of a step function and in params of pip_add(). (A formula was set as a value before; to do so now, give it as a string and turn it into a formula in the step.)
  • params of pip_add() and pip_replace() can give values to parameters of fun that have no default, so that existing functions can be steps without a wrapper, e.g. pip_add(p, "avg", mean, params = list(x = ~data, na.rm = TRUE)).
  • pip_replace() gets the argument keep_params. With TRUE, the new step keeps the current values of the unbound params that are arguments of the new function, unless params give them or the new function binds them.
  • pip_run() has a new argument map, a function like lapply() that runs the keys of a step mapped over partitions (exec = "auto"), e.g. in parallel with parallel::mclapply or future.apply::future_lapply.
  • A run can be cancelled from the progress callback of pip_run(): if it returns FALSE, the run is halted before the next step.
  • A mapped step that failed for some keys is only called for the failed keys in the next run, unless its parameters or inputs changed or the run is forced. This does not hold for a copy made by pip_clone(), which runs all keys again (known issue, #172).
  • pip_run() warns (class pipeflow_outdated_before) if a step changes itself or a done step before it via .self, as these steps then run again in the next run.
  • The step table has new columns time_start (the start of the step’s last run, also set if the run fails) and duration (how long the last run took, as a difftime). Both are NA for a step that has not run since it was added, replaced or reset, and pipelines saved with an earlier version get the columns when read.
  • The log of pip_run() names the pipeline and ends with a summary of the whole run, including restarts, e.g. Finished in 0.251 s (3 done, 1 skipped, 0 failed). The footer of print() shows the duration of the last run and the number of steps per state.
  • The option pipeflow.lgr sets the default logger of pip_run(), e.g. options(pipeflow.lgr = function(level, msg) NULL) switches logging off.
  • pip_get_params(x, simplify = FALSE) returns the values of all steps, grouped by param name and named by step, e.g. to find params whose values differ between steps.
  • pip_add(), pip_replace() and rbind() warn (class pipeflow_param_conflict) if an unbound param of a new step has another value than the same param in other steps. Turn it off with options(pipeflow.warn_param_conflicts = FALSE).
  • [ warns if the selector is a column name that is also a variable of the caller: with step <- "load", p[step] selects by the step column.
  • pip_graph(): the nodes have a title column (shown by visNetwork on hover), the edges a dashes column (a ~try() reference is dashed), and format = "mermaid" returns the graph as a mermaid flowchart, which renders e.g. on GitHub and in Quarto.

Bug fixes

  • pip_run() tracks the steps of a run by node id, so a step that changes its own pipeline via .self (or a progress callback) no longer makes the run run the wrong step, fail with “subscript out of bounds” (#157) or run the dependents of a renamed failed step with the failure as input (#160). A step that was removed during the run is skipped, and a step that renames itself keeps its output.
  • pip_run() skips a step whose input is still "new", e.g. a step added via .self during the run, instead of running it with a NULL input.
  • A step that fails in a run with on_error = "stop" stores its error as its output, as with "continue", instead of keeping the output of an earlier attempt.
  • A step function is called by the step name with its arguments as symbols, e.g. fit(x = x), so errors and pipeflow_failures no longer carry the inputs of the step in their call (megabytes of data), and an output that keeps the frame of the step call no longer keeps the pipeline.
  • A key of a partitioned output whose value is NULL is kept, and a step mapped over it gets the argument.
  • pip_lock() on a step that is not done marks its downstream steps as outdated (#147).
  • pip_reset() marks the downstream steps of the reset steps as "outdated", and on a view it keeps the time of the last run and the run state of the pipeline.
  • Setting exec or out of a step with p[[step, "exec"]] <- or p[[step, "out"]] <- (also via p[i, j] <- and views) marks the affected steps as "outdated", so the next run uses the new value. See ?Extract.pipeflow.
  • An assignment to several steps, p[i, j] <- value or p[i, ] <- q[i, ], changes all selected steps or none.
  • Copying steps with p[i] <- q[j] keeps the params given via params and resolves relative references such as ~-1 by name, also onto themselves.
  • rbind() no longer drops arguments with a NULL value from the step functions of the second pipeline, and no longer fails if it references a step with a non-syntactic name.
  • Steps with non-syntactic names, e.g. "source data", can be referenced with backticks, x = ~`source data`.
  • pip_add() and pip_rename() reject step names that start with -, which a reference ~-1 would take as a relative reference.
  • pip_rename() also renames the step in the failures of failed keys if the step name has a name attribute, e.g. if it is taken from p[["step"]].
  • p[i, view = FALSE] no longer warns that an edge already exists if a step refers to the same step with several arguments, and v[, view = FALSE] returns a standalone pipeline instead of the view.
  • pip_set_params() on a pipeline or view without steps no longer says that all selected steps are locked.

Minor improvements

  • The error messages of pip_add(), pip_remove(), pip_rename() and pip_replace() for step name, function and params are the same, e.g. pip_remove(p, "") says that the step must be a non-empty string.
  • Adding or replacing a step that references a step that comes after the insertion point reports “cannot reference steps that come after …”, and the error for a view given to pip_add(), pip_clone() or rbind() points at x[, view = FALSE].
  • The error of a mapped step whose partitioned inputs have different keys names the arguments that differ and the keys that are missing, extra or in a different order.
  • The warning of pip_set_params() about unknown params no longer shows the call.
  • Internal helpers were renamed and documented consistently, and a %||% helper is used for NULL defaults.

Documentation

  • New articles “Emulating targets features” (recipes for file tracking, rebuilds after helper changes, a tar_meta()-like table, reproducible random numbers, saved results, runs in a fresh R process and outdated steps) and “Comparison and benchmarks” (formerly “pipeflow vs targets”), and the vignettes “Annotated step outputs” and “Nested pipelines”.
  • ?as.function.pipeflow shows the error messages of inner steps, ?pip_add explains how outputs that keep an environment can keep the whole pipeline, and ?pip_view says that running a view also runs the upstream steps of its steps.
  • New hexagon logo, two-page cheat sheet (shown in the README), shorter README introduction, and a centered pkgdown site with the logo.

pipeflow 0.5.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-13

Breaking changes

  • v[["view"]] returns the names of the covered steps instead of row indices.
  • .self is only made available in step functions that refer to it, i.e. if the name .self appears in the function body.
  • pip_replace() by default now keeps the tags and the execution mode of the replaced step.

New features

  • pip_run(on_error = "continue") continues the run of unaffected steps after a step fails with an error.
  • allow mitigation of inputs from failed steps via ~try() references (x = ~try(step)), e.g. by creating fallback results for failed steps.
  • pip_param_value() is a generic for unwrapping parameter values, enabling users to set pipeline parameters that consist of non-trivial types or classes.
  • pip_set_params() gains unknown = c("warn", "ignore", "error") for parameters that no step defines, and force = TRUE to outdate steps even if the values are identical.
  • pip_run_state() returns the run state of a pipeline or view.
  • The default logger pipeflow_lgr() is exported, so custom loggers can build on it.
  • Pipelines survive saveRDS() and readRDS(), and can be sent to other R processes (see ?pip_new).

Changes

  • pip_set_params() no longer outdates steps if the values are identical to the stored ones.
  • Errors from pip_run() name the step (step 'fit': ...) and have class pipeflow_step_error with the fields step and parent. A failing partition key gives a pipeflow_key_error with key and parent.
  • Views keep the name of their pipeline (before: "<name> view").
  • Views keep track of their steps instead of row numbers, so they stay valid when steps are added, removed, renamed or replaced.
  • pip_run() also re-runs a "done" step if one of its inputs was executed in the same run.
  • A run stopped by halt() ends in run state "halted" (before: "ready").
  • pip_add() and pip_replace() warn if params contain names that are also arguments of fun.
  • print() now shows conditions, matrices, arrays, tables, functions and environments in the out column in short form, e.g. <error/simpleError>.

Bug fixes

  • Steps that never ran stay "new", and a run only outdates the steps downstream of steps it executed.
  • x[[step, j]] on a view read the wrong row.
  • Copies made by pip_clone(), p[] or p[i, view = FALSE] shared .self with the original.
  • pip_set_params() no longer warns about parameters defined only in locked steps.
  • pip_add() and pip_replace() reject primitive functions such as sum with a clear error, and pip_add() calls .self a reserved parameter name.
  • A step that references the same step more than once no longer warns about an existing edge.

Documentation

  • New vignettes “Handling failures” and “Annotated parameter values”.
  • “Get started”, “Nested pipelines”, “Self-modifying pipelines” and “Combine pipelines” cover identical values, unknown = "ignore", when .self is available, and saving pipelines.
  • The benchmark vignette was revised.
  • The package website is built by a GitHub Actions workflow on release tags.

pipeflow 0.4.0

CRAN release: 2026-09-27

New features

  • Pipeline functions can be called as methods on the pipeline object, e.g. p$add(...), p$run(...), p$set_params(...), …
  • The extract and replace operators gained new capabilities:
    • two-index extraction (p[[step, "out"]]),
    • negative row indices in p[...] and p[i, j] <- value,
    • boolean filters in p[...] (data.table-style expressions),
    • cross-pipeline assignment to copy steps between pipelines,
    • step removal via p[[step, "step"]] <- NULL,
    • time stamps via p[[step, "time"]] <- value,
    • setting or replacing views via p[["view"]] <- ....
  • pip_collect() (formerly pip_collect_out()) supports grouping via a by argument, as.table = TRUE to return a compact table, and a simplify argument to control flattening of single-step groups.
  • pip_data() provides direct access to the underlying step table.
  • pip_graph() (formerly pip_get_graph()) returns visNetwork-compatible graph data. The old function names remain available as deprecated aliases.
  • The derived columns depends, unbound and nodeId are read-only and can’t be assigned directly.
  • pip_view() gains a join = "union" argument to combine filters as a logical OR.
  • .self is now automatically available inside every step function (and is a protected parameter name), enabling pipelines to modify themselves at runtime, including .self$restart() and .self$halt().

Changes

  • The columns of the internal step table were reordered and nodeId is now shown in the full print view (cols = "all").
  • The dependencies on lgr and jsonlite were removed.

Bug fixes

  • pip_rename() no longer corrupts the parameters of single-step pipelines.
  • Running a view now resolves upstream dependencies correctly.

Documentation

  • New vignettes: “Working with pipeline views” and “Nested pipelines”.
  • Help pages of related functions were consolidated (extract/replace operators, dim/length, lock/unlock, tag/untag, set_params/get_params).
  • pip_run() documents the runtime control flow (restart(), halt()), and pip_add() gained an example for the after argument.

pipeflow 0.3.0

CRAN release: 2026-06-15

New features

  • C++ DAG engine (src/dag.cpp): All graph operations (node/edge add/remove, topological ordering, reachability queries) run at C++ speed via Rcpp, eliminating R object overhead for dependency resolution.
  • New pip_* API: Functional API replacing the R6 Pipeline class — pip_new(), pip_add(), pip_run(), pip_replace(), pip_clone(), pip_bind(), pip_view(), pip_tag()/pip_untag(), etc.
  • Execution modes (auto/split/reduce/plain): Native support for map-reduce style workflows where steps split output into named partitions and downstream steps auto-map over them.
  • Dependency validation at definition time: pip_add(), pip_replace(), and pip_remove() fail fast on broken references.
  • New pkgdown-only article pipeflow vs targets (vignettes/articles/v07-vs-targets.Rmd) with an 18-row feature comparison table and benchmarks.

Breaking changes

  • Legacy pipe_* functions and Pipeline R6 class are deprecated (preserved as aliases in R/aliases.R, R/pipelineR6.R).
  • pip_collect_out() no longer accepts grouped or by parameters. It returns a flat named list of step outputs. Use pip_view() with tags and manual list composition for grouped output.
  • The group column has been removed from the pipeline data.table. Steps previously using group = "..." in pip_add() should use tags = "...".

Documentation

  • Comprehensive revision of all vignettes to match the new pip_* API.
  • Revised vignettes/v04-collect-output.Rmd to demonstrate tag-based grouping via pip_view() composition.
  • Updated README with a “Why use {pipeflow}” feature list, a short usage example, and a revised vs-targets summary.

Internal

  • Extensive test suite covering C++ DAG, pip_* API, aliases, execution modes, and recursive runs.
  • MIT license, updated CI workflows, dependabot config, kilo.json, lintr/styler config.
